description: I’d heard stories about this happening and thought, that’s wild. I don’t believe it… What happened next was unforgettable.
transcript: I died on January 23rd, 2024. I hear about near-death experiences, and you probably hear about them all the time, and you're like, bro, that's not fucking true. I was in a skiing accident, and I journaled. So if you doubt near-death experiences, hear this. All I remember was feeling a few seconds, but also a lifetime of complete peace. I hear the click of my skis, my body compress, which felt like my neck going into my hips, then darkness. I remember seeing squares of memories, almost like a photo album on an iPhone, moving across my brain like a screen being swiped. I remember standing with my hand on a chair, wearing a black shirt, and the chair was dark wood. I was standing above what seemed like my son and a family of people I had never met, but it felt like home. I recall all of my small worries, like what I was studying in college, what people thought of me, all of my overthinking thoughts about security vanished, and I was still. It was almost like a lunge out of my body and out of my worries, something showing me everything will be all right. I remember my girlfriend at the time being there and having a feeling of needing to be held. I remember having a strong feeling of someone telling me it is not my time and I have something to do in this life that I haven't done yet. It was a white skinny dude with long curly hair that gave me a what the fuck look when I walked up the cobblestone path with a big arching cobblestone arch. I walked into the kitchen. They were preparing for dinner. He was wearing a white v-neck with a silver platter and he looks at me and says, what the fuck? And he pushed me out. I said, you're not supposed to be here. And I had the strongest urge and feeling that there wasn't even a thought that it was over and that I still had something to fulfill in my life. It was almost like I was being rejected from the light, rejected from the end, and eagerly pushed back because I had something to do. Soon after that, I opened my eyes and I didn't feel like I was in mammoth skiing. I felt like I was not inside my body. I opened my eyes and see the snow thought, Oh God, that was real. This happened to me. Then everything came back. Lightning pain up my lower back. Three pink elephants. Life changed forever. Broken back.
